chunks: "Honestly, my ECAD scripting experience is [level: e. g. light / moderate] . [What you really did: e. g.
I wrote a short Python script in KiCad to place twelve LEDs in a circle, and a separate script that reads the exported BOM and flags parts without a manufacturer part number.]

The ring placement is a good example: you loop over the parts, compute the angle as 2π i over N, set x as the centre plus r cos θ and y as r sin θ, and rotate each part by its angle so they face outward.
Doing that by hand for 12 LEDs is slow and imprecise; doing it for 60 is unreasonable.
The BOM checker groups lines by value, footprint and MPN, prints the counts, and exits with an error if any line has no part number, which I run before I send a release.
I know the other tools expose similar hooks: Altium has built-in scripting and an API, Eagle uses ULPs and script files, and Allegro uses SKILL.
I'd treat any script that modifies the board carefully: run it on a copy, check the result visually and with DRC, and keep the script in version control.
What I like about scripting is that it makes releases repeatable: the same script generates the same outputs every time."
